skill.name: typescript-strict-guard
skill.description: Guides AI assistants through strict TypeScript patterns, explicit typing, runtime guards, React typing, async handling, and local pre-validation.
skill.summary: Enforces strict TypeScript habits with focused guides, examples, and a local validation script.
skill.author: Barnhardt-Enterprises-Inc

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged many patterns because this skill is documentation-heavy and includes TypeScript examples. Manual review found the backticks, fetch calls, environment variable names, and file paths are examples or validator messages, not malicious runtime behavior. No prompt-injection attempt or exfiltration intent was found.

content.value_statement: Strict TypeScript projects fail when weak typing enters reviews or generated code. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code clear patterns for safer TypeScript output.
actual_capabilities: Explains strict mode fixes for unsafe any, @ts-ignore, non-null assertions, and implicit parameters.
Provides React TypeScript patterns for props, events, hooks, refs, contexts, and server components.
Documents type guards, assertion functions, branded types, and runtime validation examples.
Covers async typing, Result patterns, retry logic, cancellation, and error handling.
Includes a Python validator that scans TypeScript files for common strict mode violations.
limitations: It is a guidance skill, not a full TypeScript compiler or linter replacement.
The validator uses regex checks and can miss complex TypeScript parser cases.
Examples must be adapted to each project framework, dependency version, and coding standard.
It does not automatically fix code unless the host AI tool edits files.

use_cases.title: Review generated TypeScript
use_cases.description: Find strict mode problems before generated code reaches a pull request.

use_cases.title: Standardize React typing
use_cases.description: Apply consistent props, event, hook, and form patterns across React components.

use_cases.title: Harden external data handling
use_cases.description: Replace unsafe casts with type guards, assertions, and runtime validation patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Check strict mode basics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single TypeScript file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript file for strict mode issues. Identify unsafe any, @ts-ignore, non-null assertions, and missing return types.

prompt_templates.title: Improve React typings
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this React TypeScript code to use explicit props, typed events, safe refs, and precise hook return types.

prompt_templates.title: Design runtime guards
prompt_templates.scenario: External API or unknown input validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create type guards and assertion helpers for this external data shape. Avoid unsafe casts and explain each narrowing step.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a TypeScript workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this TypeScript workflow for strict mode gaps, async error typing, third-party type boundaries, and validator coverage.

output_examples.input: A React form component uses broad event types and unsafe assertions.
output: Lists the unsafe event and assertion patterns.
Recommends exact React event types and nullable state handling.
Explains how the changes satisfy strict mode.

output_examples.input: An API client returns unknown data without validation.
output: Defines the expected domain shape in plain terms.
Suggests runtime guards before returning typed values.
Adds error handling guidance for invalid responses.

output_examples.input: A project wants a pre-commit TypeScript sanity check.
output: Shows when to run the validator during review.
Notes that compiler and linter checks are still required.

best_practices: Use the guide before generating TypeScript that touches external data or React state.
Run the validator on changed files, then confirm results with TypeScript and project lint rules.
Prefer unknown plus type guards when data crosses a trust boundary.
anti_patterns: Do not treat examples as final code without adapting project-specific types.
Do not replace the TypeScript compiler, ESLint, or tests with this skill alone.
Do not silence errors with assertions when a guard or safer model is practical.

faq.question: Does this skill write TypeScript code automatically?
faq.answer: It guides the host AI tool. File edits depend on the tool and permissions in the current session.

faq.question: Can it replace TypeScript compiler checks?
faq.answer: No. Use it with the compiler, lint rules, tests, and project-specific review standards.

faq.question: Does the validator need network access?
faq.answer: No. The included Python validator scans local TypeScript files selected by the user.

faq.question: Is it useful for React projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for props, events, hooks, refs, context, forms, and server components.

faq.question: How does it handle external API data?
faq.answer: It recommends unknown input, type guards, assertion helpers, and explicit error paths before typed use.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
